summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis of CXCR2, CXCR1 and their ligand CXCL8. CXCR2 leads the deterministic convergence ranking: it is raised in all eight biopsy cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa, genetically associated in Open Targets and has clinical-stage antagonists, none established in UC. Single-cell data with neutrophils place almost all CXCR2 and CXCR1 transcripts in neutrophils, composition adjustment shrinks the CXCR2 change and removes the significance of the CXCL8 change, and in the trial cohorts high baseline CXCR2 also marks placebo non-response. The axis is therefore best read as a marker of neutrophil influx and disease severity that could also be a target on recruited neutrophils, not as a change of resident tissue.

The candidates that hold up best as tissue-level changes are those whose rise survives composition adjustment in a replicated cell of origin: MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts, DUOX2 in enterocytes (confirmed in situ), IDO1 in macrophages and dendritic cells, and CHI3L1 from a mixed epithelial, stromal and neutrophil source. None of them has genetic support, and plasma Mendelian randomisation is null for IDO1, so they are expression-led candidates that need functional validation; IDO1 is the only one with clinical-stage inhibitors.

Genetics separates causal axes from reactive ones. IL12B, the shared cytokine subunit blocked by ustekinumab, has the strongest plasma-protein Mendelian randomisation signal, risk-increasing and colocalised with IBD GWAS, while changing only modestly in biopsies: it is the positive control that bulk expression underweights. CD274 (PD-L1) is up in mucosa but higher plasma protein lowers UC risk, so blockade would be the wrong direction; CXCL5 shows the same protective direction without colocalisation, and CXCL8 has a null MR.

The most reproducible biomarkers are the loss of colonocyte metabolic, absorptive and barrier genes (HMGCS2, SLC26A2, CLDN8, AQP8), decreased in all or nearly all eight cohorts and confined to inflamed mucosa for HMGCS2, and the gain of neutrophil, antimicrobial and remodelling genes (S100A8, AQP9, CHI3L1, DUOX2, MMP3). These are markers of epithelial injury and neutrophil infiltration rather than drug targets.

At the pathway level, JAK-STAT and TNFa activity and STAT3 transcription-factor activity rise in all eight cohorts; these axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs and act as positive controls. In the trial cohorts, baseline TNFa pathway activity and genes such as CXCR2, CXCL8, TREM1 and OSM are higher in ustekinumab non-responders but are also higher in placebo non-responders or show no drug-by-placebo interaction, so they mark disease severity rather than drug-specific resistance; baseline IL23A and ITGB7 do not stratify response to the drugs that target them.

pathways.text: Pathway activity inferred from target genes is the most uniform signal across cohorts. JAK-STAT activity is raised in all eight cohorts (cohorts up [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8]) and TNFa and NFkB in every cohort, strongest in UNIFI (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]); STAT3 is among the strongest inferred transcription-factor activities (UNIFI t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]) and the AP1 complex is also up everywhere. These are axes already targeted by approved UC drugs (anti-TNF, JAK inhibitors, anti-cytokine antibodies acting upstream of STAT3), so they validate the method rather than reveal new leads. WNT is up in most cohorts (cohorts up [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=7]) and hypoxia in all, broad tissue-response signals.

Not every pathway is consistent: p53 decreases in only a minority of cohorts (cohorts down [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_down=3]) and the Androgen pathway has opposite signs across cohorts, so neither should be called a UC-wide pathway. Pathway scores from bulk biopsies also cannot separate tissue change from changes in cell composition.

Among cell-cell circuits in the single-cell data with neutrophils, the most specific inflamed-mucosa circuit is CXCL8 sent by neutrophils (Neutrophil CXCR4 state) to ACKR1 on endothelial cells (inflamed score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993]), a plausible route for presenting chemokine and recruiting neutrophils, with a self-amplifying neutrophil-to-neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2 loop alongside it (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]). This axis is untargeted in UC. Other circuits are weak: neutrophil OSM to IL6ST on lamina propria fibroblasts decreases in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]); IL1B pairs only with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils, scoring zero in non-inflamed tissue (score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_noninflamed=0]) so its change has no finite magnitude; and TREM1 has no ligand-receptor pair passing thresholds, so its sender and receiver cannot be assigned. These scores are co-expression, not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: In the trial cohorts, the neutrophil and inflammatory genes associate with non-response mainly to ustekinumab. Higher baseline CXCR2 marks ustekinumab non-response (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but also UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]); CXCL8 behaves the same (ustekinumab padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102], placebo padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]), as does TREM1 (ustekinumab padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474], placebo padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]). TNFa pathway activity is higher in non-responders to several drugs, for infliximab with BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294], but also in placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]). With no significant drug-by-placebo interaction, these are markers of general severity, not drug-specific resistance.

Drug-specific signals are scarce. OSM associates with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) and is the one gene whose UNIFI placebo association is not significant (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), yet its interaction test is not significant either, and in golimumab nothing survives correction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]). JAK-STAT activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not in vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]). Negative results matter: baseline IL23A does not predict ustekinumab outcome (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]) and ITGB7 does not predict vedolizumab outcome (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), so target expression does not stratify response to the drug that blocks it. The infliximab and vedolizumab arms are small, so non-significance there is weak evidence of absence.

discovery.text: CHRDL2, a secreted BMP antagonist, is the strongest first-in-class candidate in the discovery screen: up in all eight cohorts, antibody-tractable and stromal, with inflammatory fibroblasts the top inflamed cluster. Its weaknesses are composition and safety: only a minority of the bulk rise is retained after composition adjustment (retained fraction [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]), and its highest vital-organ RNA is the largest among the top candidates (nTPM [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6]). It is a hypothesis that needs fibroblast-level functional work and protein-level safety data.

CPXM1, a stromal carboxypeptidase-like protein, is antibody-tractable, up in all eight cohorts and has low vital-organ expression (nTPM [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1]), the best safety profile among the stromal candidates. It is only partly retained after composition adjustment, few UC papers mention it, and there is no drug or functional validation.

XKR9 is the only top discovery candidate classified as intrinsic and epithelial (enterocytes and goblet cells), with most of its bulk increase retained after adjustment (retained fraction [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.798]). Its replication is weaker, up in only four cohorts, and few cells express it, so it needs confirmation in more cohorts before validation work.

LAX1 illustrates a discovery candidate that is mostly infiltrate: it is lymphocyte-derived (plasma cells the top inflamed cluster, with a lineage that does not replicate between datasets) and little of its rise survives adjustment (retained fraction [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.230]), so it marks immune infiltration rather than a tissue-intrinsic change.

integration.text: The streams agree most on the neutrophil axis and the epithelial loss. CXCR2, CXCR1 and CXCL8 are reproducible in expression, local to inflamed mucosa, genetically associated for the receptors and drug-tractable, but single-cell, composition and treatment-response data all say the same thing: the signal comes from recruited neutrophils and tracks severity. The epithelial loss genes (HMGCS2, SLC26A2, CLDN8) agree across expression, inflammation and literature as biomarkers. The pathway stream agrees with approved drug classes: JAK-STAT and TNFa activity are positive controls, as is the strong Mendelian randomisation signal for IL12B.

The streams disagree in three places. First, the genes with the largest and most cell-intrinsic expression changes (MMP1, DUOX2, CHI3L1, IDO1) have no genetic support and, where testable, null Mendelian randomisation, while the strongest genetic signals (IL12B, IL10, JAK2) change little in bulk tissue. Second, CD274 and CXCL5 are raised in mucosa but plasma MR places higher protein on the protective side, so mucosal rise may be compensatory and inhibition is not supported. Third, the literature stream is thin exactly where convergence is highest: CXCR2 and CD274 have no extracted relations, and support for IDO1, CHI3L1 and AQP9 is preclinical.

literature.text: Verbatim-validated literature relations give mechanistic support to a few expression-led candidates, each from one or two recent studies. IDO1 is reported elevated in UC, drives M1 macrophage polarization through the GRP78-XBP1 endoplasmic-reticulum stress pathway, and a methyl-tryptophan IDO inhibitor ameliorated DSS colitis. CHI3L1 correlates with NLRP3 inflammasome expression and promotes macrophage pyroptosis through BCAT1 and NF-kappaB, with velpatasvir identified as a binding repurposing hit. AQP9, predominantly neutrophil-expressed, promotes neutrophil extracellular trap formation through JAK2-STAT3-mediated pyroptosis in mouse colitis. DUOX2 is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed UC biopsies, and MMP10 is raised in active and even prediagnostic UC. All of this is preclinical or biomarker evidence; none of these genes has clinical UC data.

The literature stream is uneven. CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking but the corpus holds no extracted relation for it, only a hub-gene mention, and CD274 likewise appears only as a macrophage-infiltration hub gene, so their literature component comes from Open Targets. Much of the biomarker literature for MMP1, SLC26A2, S100A9 and LCN2 is bioinformatic or single-study diagnostic work; SLC26A2 loss correlates with Mayo score and PUCAI. The most clinically relevant relation links the inflammatory signature to treatment failure: in tofacitinib non-responders, activated macrophages and fibroblasts upregulated IL1B together with MMP9, IL6, CXCL1, CXCL8 and S100A9, a signal from infiltrating and activated cells rather than epithelium.

external.text: Known UC targets appear as positive controls. IL12B, the subunit blocked by ustekinumab, has the strongest plasma-pQTL Mendelian randomisation signal: higher protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]) and colocalises with IBD GWAS, while its biopsy change is small (meta log2FC [gene=IL12B; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.436]). JAK2 carries strong Open Targets genetic association and approved inhibitors. Among non-approved candidates, CXCR2 and CXCR1 combine Open Targets genetic association with clinical-stage dual antagonists developed for other indications; CXCR2 has no cis-pQTL, so MR could not test it. FCGR2A has strong genetic association and a modest expression rise but no drug.

The expression-led candidates lack causal genetic support. CXCL8 has no Open Targets genetic association and a null plasma MR (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]); IDO1 has clinical-stage inhibitors from oncology but also a null MR (p [gene=IDO1; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.111]); MMP1, CHI3L1 and DUOX2 have no genetic association. Two genes point the other way: higher plasma PD-L1 lowers UC risk (CD274 OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595], colocalised), so checkpoint blockade would be the wrong direction, and higher CXCL5 also lowers risk (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]) without colocalisation. IL10 has a protective MR estimate from a single instrument (OR per SD [gene=IL10; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.071]) that should not be taken literally. Plasma MR measures circulating protein, not mucosal protein, so a null MR does not exclude a local role.

cells.text: Single-cell data separate tissue changes from cell influx. In the dataset with neutrophils, CXCR2 and CXCR1 transcripts in inflamed mucosa are almost entirely neutrophil-derived (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965] and [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962]), as are most CXCL8 ([gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]), S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]) and IL1B ([gene=IL1B; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.702]) transcripts; TREM1 is also largely neutrophil-derived. Smillie, which captured no neutrophils, assigns CXCR2 to T/NK cells, so its attribution does not replicate and genes of neutrophil origin are misattributed there. These neutrophil genes are markers of inflammation rather than targets in a resident cell type.

Composition adjustment of the bulk biopsies confirms this split. CXCL8 loses significance after adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]) and so does IL1B ([gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0728]); CXCR2 shrinks to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409], while AQP9 ([gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]) and S100A8 ([gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]) keep a residual change. In contrast, MMP1 ([gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]), DUOX2 ([gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]), CHI3L1 ([gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]) and IDO1 ([gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]) remain significant. The adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so loss of significance is not proof of pure influx, whereas retention is good evidence of a tissue change.

The cell of origin of the tissue-level candidates replicates across datasets. MMP1 is a stromal product, with inflammatory fibroblasts the top inflamed cluster (share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531]); DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes, lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]); IDO1 is made by macrophages and dendritic cells; CHI3L1 has a mixed origin with neutrophils contributing under half. In situ, DUOX2 is confirmed in epithelium by Xenium single cells and Visium spots, while for MMP1 the Visium fibroblast score co-varies only weakly with it across spots (rho [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium; source=DATASET:GSE189184; compartment_rho=0.191]) and MMP1 is not on the Xenium panel, so the fibroblast attribution rests mainly on dissociated single cells.

inflammation.text: Within the same patients (MSCCR, paired inflamed vs non-inflamed biopsies), the neutrophil and remodelling genes are clearly local to inflamed mucosa: CXCR2 rises by a paired log2FC of [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], CXCL8 by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.968] and MMP3 by [gene=MMP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.3368]. The loss of HMGCS2 is also local: in non-inflamed mucosa it is essentially unchanged from controls, log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649], so the epithelial metabolic loss accompanies active inflammation rather than preceding it.

A smaller component is already present in non-inflamed UC mucosa. CXCR2 is modestly raised in non-inflamed mucosa versus controls, log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399], and so is DUOX2, log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8129], so part of the DUOX2 signal may reflect the disease state rather than current inflammation. The paired and non-inflamed contrasts exist only in MSCCR, so this pattern is not replicated in the other cohorts.

replication.text: The discovery cohort's leading changes reproduce well in the four microarray cohorts (UNIFI, PURSUIT-SC and the two Leuven cohorts) and the three further RNA-seq cohorts (PROTECT, RISK and an adult colon cohort): nearly all leading convergence genes change in the same direction and significantly in all eight. For example, CXCL8 rises by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=2.2841] in the MSCCR discovery cohort, by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE92415; layer=rna; cohort=GSE92415; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=3.9974] in PURSUIT-SC and by [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE109142; layer=rna; cohort=GSE109142; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=4.6322] in paediatric PROTECT, and HMGCS2 falls by [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-2.1465] in MSCCR, by [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE73661; layer=rna; cohort=GSE73661; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=-4.7239] in the Leuven infliximab/vedolizumab cohort and by [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE165512; layer=rna; cohort=GSE165512; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=-4.2601] in adult colon. REG1A is the main exception among large changes: up but not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]) or in the adult colon cohort. Effect sizes differ between platforms and contrasts, so replication is judged on direction and significance rather than magnitude.

expression.text: Across the eight-cohort random-effects meta-analysis, the largest and most reproducible increases in UC mucosa are neutrophil-recruitment, antimicrobial and remodelling genes. The neutrophil chemokine CXCL8 rises by a pooled log2FC of [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864], the secreted chitinase-like protein CHI3L1 by [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.875], the calprotectin subunit S100A8 by [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.7697], the epithelial oxidase DUOX2 by [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4116] and the stromelysin MMP3 by [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.9012], each in the same direction in all eight cohorts. MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10 follow the same pattern, a tissue-remodelling signature.

The strongest decreases describe a loss of colonocyte metabolism, absorption and barrier. The water channel AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss, log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]; the tight-junction gene CLDN8 falls by [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.291], the ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2 by [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.8375] and the sulfate transporter SLC26A2 by [gene=SLC26A2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.495], all decreased in all or nearly all of the eight cohorts. The chloride-bicarbonate exchanger SLC26A3 is a smaller but consistent loss, log2FC [gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702], and is the rare lost epithelial gene with UC genetic association. Together with the gain of antimicrobial and neutrophil genes, this describes a mucosa that loses colonocyte function while recruiting neutrophils; these are biomarkers of epithelial injury, and any therapy would have to restore rather than inhibit them.

The top-ranked convergence genes are not the largest fold changes. CXCR2 rises by a pooled log2FC of [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], smaller than its ligand, but in all eight cohorts; JAK2, ranked on genetics and approved inhibitors, changes only by [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874], although consistently. Conversely REG1A has a large pooled increase, log2FC [gene=REG1A; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4862], but is significant in only six of eight cohorts. Between-cohort heterogeneity is high for most top genes, so pooled fold changes describe direction and rough size only.

targets.rationale: Positive control: the subunit blocked by the approved UC drug ustekinumab, with the strongest risk-increasing plasma-pQTL Mendelian randomisation signal, colocalised with IBD GWAS. Placed first despite a low numeric convergence rank because the ranking is dominated by bulk expression, where IL12B changes little; causal genetics plus clinical efficacy outweighs expression.

Top of the convergence ranking: up in all eight cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa, Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage dual CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists. Single-cell and composition data show a neutrophil-influx signal and it marks placebo non-response too, so it is a target on recruited neutrophils and a severity biomarker rather than a tissue target; no cis-pQTL, so MR is untested.
Positive control: strong Open Targets genetic association and approved JAK inhibitors, with a modest but consistent expression rise and JAK-STAT pathway activity raised in all eight cohorts.

Best-supported tissue-intrinsic candidate: up in all eight cohorts, made by inflammatory fibroblasts with replicated attribution, and still significant after composition adjustment. Ranked above other expression genes for that reason, but genetics are absent and MR is null, and broad MMP inhibitors failed elsewhere for toxicity, so a selective agent would be needed.

Consistently up, myeloid-derived with replicated attribution and retained after composition adjustment; preclinical literature links it to M1 polarization and an IDO inhibitor improved DSS colitis, and clinical-stage inhibitors exist from oncology. Null MR and no genetics keep it below MMP1.

Epithelial oxidase, up in all eight cohorts, epithelial origin replicated and confirmed in situ, retained after adjustment and partly present in non-inflamed mucosa. A strong activity biomarker of the inflamed epithelium; as a target it lacks genetics and a drug.

Among the largest and most replicated increases, mixed cellular origin, retained after adjustment, with preclinical evidence for macrophage pyroptosis via BCAT1 and NF-kappaB. No drug and no genetic association, so mainly a biomarker with an exploratory target case.

Large, eight-cohort increase but neutrophil-derived, not significant after composition adjustment, null MR, and a severity marker in placebo arms too. Ranked third numerically, but placed lower here because every independent stream points to an influx marker rather than a causal target.

Up in all eight cohorts with genetic association, but MR shows higher PD-L1 protein lowers UC risk with colocalisation, so the mucosal rise is likely protective and only checkpoint agonism, not blockade, would be logical. Kept as a mechanism-led target with the direction flagged.
Most reproducible loss marker: down in all eight cohorts and unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa, so it reports active epithelial injury; a target would require restoring function.

Calprotectin subunit, strongly up in all eight cohorts and mostly neutrophil-derived with a residual change after adjustment: a neutrophil-activity biomarker, consistent with its clinical use as faecal calprotectin, not a tissue target.

Strong Open Targets genetic association with a significant but modest expression rise; no drug and only predicted tractability. Included because genetics plus expression is rare among the top genes, but cell source and MR were not examined.

Exploratory: strongest first-in-class candidate, up in all eight cohorts, antibody-tractable and fibroblast-derived, but mostly composition-dependent and with the highest vital-organ RNA among the candidates; a hypothesis for fibroblast functional validation.
Exploratory: stromal, antibody-tractable, up in all eight cohorts with low vital-organ expression; only partly composition-retained and without functional data or a drug.

limitations.text: Bulk biopsy expression mixes tissue change with immune-cell influx; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells are activated, so losing significance after adjustment is not proof of pure influx.
Paired inflamed versus non-inflamed and non-inflamed versus control contrasts exist only in the MSCCR discovery cohort, so the local-versus-global inflammation pattern is not replicated.
Pooled meta-analysis fold changes have high between-cohort heterogeneity and mix microarray and RNA-seq platforms; direction and significance are more reliable than magnitude.
Only one single-cell dataset captures neutrophils; the other misattributes neutrophil genes, and ligand-receptor scores are co-expression, not proof of signalling.
Plasma-protein Mendelian randomisation tests circulating protein, not mucosal protein, and was run for a limited set of genes; CXCR2, CXCR1 and IL1B have no cis-pQTL and were untested.

The literature corpus is small and several top genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CD274, FCGR2A, JAK2, TREM1) have no extracted relations; most literature support is bioinformatic or preclinical. The PubMed connector was not authorised and was not used.

Treatment-response arms for infliximab and vedolizumab are small, and no drug-by-placebo interaction is significant, so no response marker is drug-specific; associations are not validated predictions.
Discovery candidates lack functional validation and genetic support, and the vital-organ safety filter uses RNA only.
Passing the automatic verification means no failure was detected in evidence linkage and numeric binding; it does not validate causal interpretations or efficacy.
